subject: Vendor questionnaire: SIG vs CAIQ — form choice, evidence timeline
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@medivance.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medivance.com
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — security / SOC 2 questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo today — it was helpful. As we discussed, the security team needs guidance on which questionnaire to fill out so we can move to a formal security review. Two quick asks from my side: 

1) Do you prefer us to complete the SIG Lite (short) or the full CAIQ? We want to minimize back-and-forth but also surface the right controls.
2) If we go SIG, can you confirm which evidence you typically require up front (SOC 2 redacted, network diagrams, encryption key ownership)?

Can we target next-week delivery for an initial pass? If SIG is the right call, we can have a technical resource and our security engineer (cc’d) work with yours.

Best,
Alex
Alex Chen
Head of IT Security
Medivance Inc.
attachments: none
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@medivance.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — security / SOC 2 questions

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and for looping in your security engineer. Quick answers and proposed next steps below.

Short answers:
- SIG Lite is usually sufficient to start for commercial SaaS integrations; it gets us most of the surface controls in a compact form.
- Required up-front evidence: redacted SOC 2 (if available), a host-level diagram showing where inference instances run, and a short note on data residency (where customer data persists).

Proposed plan (suggested timeline):
- Today: we attach a SIG-quickstart pack (short guidance) + our preferred field mapping (see attachment).
- By Nov 19 (EOD): Medivance submits SIG Lite prefilling where you can; mark any gaps as "TBD".
- Nov 20–21: Redwood security (Karthik) will review the prefills, request clarifications, and list exact evidence items.
- Nov 24: target to hand off to compliance for deeper review if SOC 2 sighted or to schedule a short follow-up call.

If you'd rather start with CAIQ because you have an internal process that mandates it, we can accept that too but expect a slightly longer turnaround.

I’m happy to hop on a 20-minute call to align on evidence expectations — Jordan will coordinate scheduling.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
attachments: SIG-quickstart.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@medivance.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medivance.com, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 08:54:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — security / SOC 2 questions

Irene, Jordan — thanks. A couple of clarifying questions from our security engineer (cc’d):

- SOC 2: We have an in-progress SOC 2 Type II report due Q1. For the prefilling step, is a SOC 2 Type I or an in-progress report acceptable, or do you require the completed Type II?
- Hosting: our procurement policy needs explicit confirmation whether Redwood ever sees unredacted customer content in logs or crash reports. Can you provide a short statement on log redaction practices?

We can aim for Nov 19 initial prefills — will do SIG Lite unless you say otherwise. Also can you confirm the preferred file format for prefill (Excel / CSV / Google Sheet)?

Appreciate the cadence; if you have a one-pager on evidence expectations that would help accelerate our internal approvals.

–Alex
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@medivance.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — security / SOC 2 questions

Alex — quick answers below, and I attached a redacted SOC 2 example we share with prospects.

- SOC 2: A Type I or in-progress Type II is fine for the initial SIG prefilling. For full acceptance in procurement we typically expect Type II, but we don’t block the questionnaire process on that.
- Log redaction: Redwood’s hosted offering does not surface unredacted customer content to staff. We collect operational telemetry and token metadata for routing/costing; any customer content in logs is redacted at the first-hop (see attached excerpt). If customers enable advanced debug traces we provide a documented process and require a JIT access request and approval.
- Prefill format: Google Sheet is easiest (we maintain a mapping template); we included a prefill sheet link in the Drive link Irene shared.

Attachments: SOC2-report-redacted.pdf (redacted, pdf)

Jordan — if you could send a 20-minute slot for next week, we’ll block time to walk through the prefill template with Medivance’s security engineer.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
